newsitem.title: USA: NJ judge appoints lawyer for fetus in case.
newsitem.headline: NJ judge appoints lawyer for fetus in case.

text.p: A New Jersey judge, weighing the case of a jailed pregnant woman seeking an abortion, has ruled that the foetus has a right to an attorney, lawyers said Thursday.
Superior Court Judge Leonard Arnold appointed a lawyer to represent the 5-month-old foetus of Sonya Jackson, who is being held in the Somerset County, New Jersey, jail on drug charges.
Jackson has asked for a bail reduction to enable her to obtain an abortion.
"I have decided that the unborn child requires representation," the judge said in his ruling on Wednesday. He also suggested that the woman would need state permission to end her pregnancy.
Jackson's attorney Regina Lynch disputed the judge's opinion, saying a doctor, but not her client, may need permission to perform the abortion.
Susan Atwood, president of the New Jersey chapter of the National Organisation for Women, said Thursday that the judge was on shaky legal ground.
"New Jersey doesn't have a law restricting abortion," she said. "I am concerned that this woman is being denied her constitutional rights by the judge."

Jackson, 33, was arrested on Jan. 7 on charges of selling heroin worth $200 to an undercover police officer in Bernards Township, New Jersey, according to court documents. She is being held on $35,000 bail.
The judge appointed Richard Collier, an attorney who has represented anti-abortion groups in the past, to represent the foetus.
